# 🔐 User Login API Documentation

## Endpoint

```
POST /api/user/login

 ```

## Base URL

```
http://localhost:8000/api/user/login

 ```

---

## Description

Authenticates a user using email and password, and returns:

- Access Token (in Authorization header)
    
- Refresh Token (in HTTP-only cookie)
    
- User role
    
- First time login status
    

---

## Authentication

Required: ❌ No

(This is the login endpoint)

---

## Headers

```
Content-Type: application/json

 ```

---

## Request Body (JSON)

```
{
  "email": "john@gmail.com",
  "password": "12345678"
}

 ```

---

## Field Explanation

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| email | String | ✅ | Registered email |
| password | String | ✅ | User password |

---

## Success Response

Status: **200 OK**

Headers:

```
Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>
Set-Cookie: refreshToken=<refreshToken>; HttpOnly

 ```

Body:

```
{
  "status": "success",
  "message": "Login successful",
  "data": {
    "role": "user",
    "firstTimeLogin": true
  }
}

 ```

---

## Important: Tokens Location

### Access Token

Returned in response header:

```
Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9...

 ```

Use this token for protected routes.

---

### Refresh Token

Stored in cookie:

```
refreshToken=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9...

 ```

Used to generate new access token.

---

# Error Responses

---

## Missing email or password

Status: **400 Bad Request**

```
{
  "status": "fail",
  "message": "Email and password are required"
}

 ```

---

## Invalid email

Status: **401 Unauthorized**

```
{
  "status": "fail",
  "message": "Email or password incorrect"
}

 ```

---

## Invalid password

Status: **401 Unauthorized**

```
{
  "status": "fail",
  "message": "Email or password incorrect"
}

 ```

---

# Postman Setup Instructions

---

## Step 1: Create request

Method:

```
POST

 ```

URL:

```
http://localhost:3000/api/user/login

 ```

---

## Step 2: Headers

```
Content-Type: application/json

 ```

---

## Step 3: Body → raw → JSON

```
{
  "email": "john@gmail.com",
  "password": "12345678"
}

 ```

---

## Step 4: Click Send

---

## Step 5: Copy Access Token

From response Headers:

```
Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9...

 ```

Use in other APIs:

```
Authorization: Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN

 ```

---

# What happens internally

When login succeeds:

✔ Password compared using bcrypt

✔ Access token generated

✔ Refresh token generated

✔ Refresh token saved in database

✔ Refresh token stored in HTTP-only cookie

✔ Access token returned in Authorization header

---

# Example Database Change After Login

```
{
  "_id": "65d3f8a2c123456789abcd12",
  "email": "john@gmail.com",
  "refreshToken": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..."
}

 ```

Creates a new user with default avatar and hashed password.

| email | String | ✅ | ✅ | Valid email address |
| password | String | ✅ | ❌ | Will be hashed automatically |
| phoneNumber | String | ✅ | ✅ | Must be 10 digits |
| location | String | ✅ | ❌ | User location |
| bio | String | ❌ | ❌ | User description |
| employeId | String | ✅ | ✅ | Employee ID |

✔ User saved in MongoDB

# 👥 Get All Users API Documentation

## Endpoint

```
GET /api/getAllUsers

 ```

## Base URL

```
http://localhost:8000/api/getAllUsers

 ```

---

## Description

Fetch all users with:

- Pagination
    
- Sorting
    
- Password, refreshToken, firstTimeLogin excluded
    
- Admin access only
    

---

## Authorization

Required: ✅ Yes  
  
Role Required: ✅ Admin

Header:

```
Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>

 ```

---

## Headers

```
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN

 ```

---

# Query Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| page | Number | ❌ | 1 | Page number |
| sort | String | ❌ | recent | Sort users |

---

# Sort Options

| Value | Description |
| --- | --- |
| name-asc | Name ascending |
| name-desc | Name descending |
| oldest | Oldest users first |
| recent | Newest users first |

---

# Request Examples

---

## Default request

```
GET http://localhost:3000/api/getAllUsers

 ```

---

## Page 2

```
GET http://localhost:3000/api/getAllUsers?page=2

 ```

---

## Sort by name ascending

```
GET http://localhost:3000/api/getAllUsers?sort=name-asc

 ```

---

## Sort by newest users

```
GET http://localhost:3000/api/getAllUsers?sort=recent

 ```

---

## Combined example

```
GET http://localhost:3000/api/getAllUsers?page=1&sort=name-desc

 ```

---

# Success Response

Status: **200 OK**

```
{
  "status": "success",
  "results": 2,
  "users": [
    {
      "_id": "65d3f8a2c123456789abcd12",
      "name": "john_doe",
      "email": "john@gmail.com",
      "phoneNumber": "0912345678",
      "location": "Addis Ababa",
      "bio": "Software developer",
      "employeId": "EMP001",
      "department": "IT",
      "role": "user",
      "photo": "/images/UserPhotos/1708343434343-UserAvatar.png",
      "createdDate": "2026-02-19T10:00:00.000Z"
    },
    {
      "_id": "65d3f8a2c123456789abcd13",
      "name": "admin_user",
      "email": "admin@gmail.com",
      "phoneNumber": "0912345679",
      "location": "Addis Ababa",
      "bio": "System admin",
      "employeId": "EMP002",
      "department": "Admin",
      "role": "admin",
      "photo": "/images/UserPhotos/1708343434343-UserAvatar.png",
      "createdDate": "2026-02-18T09:00:00.000Z"
    }
  ]
}

 ```

---

# What is excluded from response

These fields are hidden:

```
password
refreshToken
firstTimeLogin

 ```

---

# Pagination Logic

```
page=1 → users 1–10
page=2 → users 11–20
page=3 → users 21–30

 ```

Limit is fixed to:

```
10 users per page

 ```

---

# Error Responses

---

## Unauthorized

Status: **401**

```
{
  "status": "fail",
  "message": "Unauthorized"
}

 ```

---

## Forbidden (Not Admin)

```
{
  "status": "fail",
  "message": "Access denied"
}

 ```

---

 ```

 ```

---

```
Authorization: Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN

 ```

## Step 4

---

# Important Bug Fix (You must fix)

Your code uses:

```
case 'name-asc': sortOption = { fullName: 1 };
case 'name-desc': sortOption = { fullName: -1 };

 ```

But your schema uses:

```
name: { type: String }

 ```

Fix it to:

```
case 'name-asc': sortOption = { name: 1 }; break;
case 'name-desc': sortOption = { name: -1 }; break;

 ```

---

# Correct Version

```
switch (req.query.sort) {
  case 'name-asc': sortOption = { name: 1 }; break;
  case 'name-desc': sortOption = { name: -1 }; break;
  case 'oldest': sortOption = { createdDate: 1 }; break;
  case 'recent': sortOption = { createdDate: -1 }; break;
  default: sortOption = { createdDate: -1 };
}

 ```

# ✏️ Update User API Documentation

## Endpoint

```
PUT /api/updateUser/:id

 ```

## Base URL

```
http://localhost:8000/api/updateUser/:id

 ```

Example:

```
http://localhost:8000/api/updateUser/65d3f8a2c123456789abcd12

 ```

---

## Description

Update a user’s information by ID.

- Admin only
    
- Password will be hashed automatically if updated
    
- Photo cannot be updated via this route (use upload-photo endpoint)
    

---

## Authorization

Required: ✅ Yes

Role Required: ✅ Admin

Header:

```
Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>

 ```

---

## Headers

```
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN

 ```

---

## URL Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| id | String | ✅ | MongoDB User ID to update |

---

## Request Body (JSON)

Include only the fields you want to update:

```
{
  "name": "john_doe_updated",
  "email": "john_new@gmail.com",
  "password": "newpassword123",
  "phoneNumber": "0912345678",
  "location": "Addis Ababa",
  "bio": "Updated bio",
  "employeId": "EMP001",
  "department": "IT",
  "role": "user"
}

 ```

⚠️ Do **not** include `photo` in body — it is ignored. Use the `/upload-photo` endpoint to update photos.

---

## Field Explanation

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| name | String | ❌ | User full name |
| email | String | ❌ | Must be unique |
| password | String | ❌ | Will be hashed automatically |
| phoneNumber | String | ❌ | Must be unique, 10 digits |
| location | String | ❌ | User location |
| bio | String | ❌ | User description |
| employeId | String | ❌ | Must be unique |
| department | String | ❌ | Department |
| role | String | ❌ | Values: `admin`, `user` |

---

## Success Response

Status: **200 OK**

```
{
  "status": "success",
  "message": "User updated successfully.",
  "user": {
    "id": "65d3f8a2c123456789abcd12",
    "fullName": "john_doe_updated",
    "email": "john_new@gmail.com",
    "role": "user",
    "photo": "/images/UserPhotos/1708343434343-UserAvatar.png"
  }
}

 ```

⚠️ Note: Your controller returns `fullName`, but your schema uses `name`. You should update the controller to `updatedUser.name` to match the schema:

```
user: {
  id: updatedUser._id,
  name: updatedUser.name,
  email: updatedUser.email,
  role: updatedUser.role,
  photo: updatedUser.photo,
}

 ```

---

## Error Responses

---

### Unauthorized (No Token)

Status: **401 Unauthorized**

```
{
  "status": "fail",
  "message": "Unauthorized"
}

 ```

---

### Forbidden (Not Admin)

Status: **403 Forbidden**

```
{
  "status": "fail",
  "message": "Access denied"
}

 ```

---

### User Not Found

Status: **404 Not Found**

```
{
  "status": "fail",
  "message": "No user found with ID 65d3f8a2c123456789abcd12"
}

 ```

---

### Validation Error

Status: **400 Bad Request**

```
{
  "status": "fail",
  "message": "User validation failed",
  "errors": {
    "email": "Email already exists"
  }
}

 ```

---

## Postman Setup Instructions

1. Method: `PUT`
    
2. URL: `http://localhost:3000/api/updateUser/USER_ID`
    
3. Content-Type: application/jsonAuthorization: Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN
    
4. Body → raw → JSON: Include the fields you want to update
    
5. Click **Send**

# 👤 Get Current User API Documentation

## Endpoint

```
GET /api/getme

 ```

## Base URL

```
http://localhost:3000/api/getme

 ```

---

## Description

Fetches the currently authenticated user’s information.

- Requires a valid access token
    
- Returns limited user info (excluding password, refreshToken, etc.)
    

---

## Authorization

Required: ✅ Yes  
  
Role Required: ❌ (any logged-in user)

Header:

```
Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>

 ```

---

## Headers

```
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN

 ```

---

## Request Parameters

No URL parameters required.

The API automatically identifies the user from the `verifyToken` middleware (using `req.userId`).

---

## Success Response

Status: **200 OK**

```
{
  "status": "success",
  "user": {
    "id": "65d3f8a2c123456789abcd12",
    "fullName": "john_doe",
    "email": "john@gmail.com",
    "role": "user",
    "photo": "/images/UserPhotos/1708343434343-UserAvatar.png"
  }
}

 ```

> 

⚠️ Note: Your controller uses `fullName` but your schema uses `name`. Update controller to `user.name` for consistency.

 
  

---

## Standard Error Responses

### Unauthorized (No Token)

```
{
  "status": "fail",
  "statusCode": 401,
  "message": "Unauthorized"
}

 ```

### User Not Found

```
{
  "status": "fail",
  "statusCode": 404,
  "message": "User not found"
}

 ```

### Cast Error / Invalid ID (handled by centralized error handler)

```
{
  "status": "error",
  "statusCode": 400,
  "message": "Invalid id: 65d3f8a2c123ZZZ.",
  "fields": ["id"]
}

 ```

# 📸 Upload User Photo API Documentation

## Endpoint

```
POST /api/upload-photo

 ```

## Base URL

```
http://localhost:8000/api/upload-photo

 ```

---

## Description

Allows the currently authenticated user to upload or update their profile photo.

- Existing photo will be deleted from the server
    
- Only one file allowed per request
    
- File size limited to 2MB (Multer limits enforced)
    

---

## Authorization

Required: ✅ Yes

Role Required: ❌ (any logged-in user)

Header:

```
Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>

 ```

---

## Headers

```
Authorization: Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN
Content-Type: multipart/form-data

 ```

---

## Request Body

### Add Gallery Entry (POST)

This endpoint handles the mixed upload of a **cover image** and an **array of gallery images**, creating a structured record in the database.

- **URL:** `{{base_url}}/api/addGallery`
    
- **Method:** `POST`
    
- **Auth:** `Bearer Token` (Required)
    
- **Body Type:** `form-data`
    

---

### 📥 Request Body (form-data)

| **coverImage** | **File** | `main_front.jpg` | **Required.** The primary display image (Max 2MB). |  
| **images** | **File** | `[Multiple Files]` | **Optional.** Select multiple files to populate the gallery array. |  
| **catagory** | Text | `Engineering` | **Required.** The group/category for the entry. |  
| **status** | Text | `Active` | Options: `Active` or `Inactive` (Defaults to Inactive). |

---

### ✅ Success Response (201 Created)

JSON

```
{
  "status": "success",
  "data": {
    "_id": "65d8f2a1b3c4d5e6f7g8h9i0",
    "coverImage": "/GaImageGallery/main_front-1715832000.jpg",
    "images": [
      "/GaImageGallery/detail1-1715832001.jpg",

    ],

    "status": "Active",

}
 ```

### ❌ Possible Errors

Managed by your `globalErrorHandler` and Multer limits:

| **Status Code** | **Message** | **Scenario** |  
| **400** | `Please upload a cover image.` | The `coverImage` field was empty or missing. |  
| **400** | `coverImage size exceeds 2MB limit.` | One of your files is larger than the 2MB limit set in `fileUpload.js`. |  
| **400** | `Too many files uploaded for field "images".` | You attempted to upload more than 10 images at once. |  
| **401** | `Unauthorized` | Missing or expired JWT token in the Authorization header. |

2. In **Headers**, add `Authorization: Bearer` .

### Get All Gallery Entries (GET)

This endpoint fetches a list of gallery entries with built-in pagination. It returns the total number of records available in the database to help the frontend calculate how many pages to display.

- **URL:** `{{base_url}}/api/getAllgallery`
    
- **Method:** `GET`
    
- **Auth:** None (Public)
    

---

### 🔍 Query Parameters

Add these to the **Params** tab in Postman to control which results you see:

| **Parameter** | **Type** | **Default** | **Description** |
| **`page`** | Number | `1` | The specific page of results you want to view. |

---

### ✅ Success Response (200 OK)

The response is structured to provide both the metadata (`total`) and the actual gallery items (`data`).

JSON

```
{
  "status": "success",
  "total": 45,
  "data": [
    {
      "_id": "65d8f2a1b3c4d5e6f7g8h9i0",
      "coverImage": "/GaImageGallery/bridge_design-1715832000.jpg",
      "images": [
        "/GaImageGallery/blueprint1-1715832001.jpg",
        "/GaImageGallery/site_photo-1715832002.jpg"
      ],
      "catagory": "Civil Engineering",
      "fileType": "image",
      "status": "Active",
      "Date": "2026-02-26T10:00:00.000Z"
    }
  ]
}

 ```

---

### 🛠 Technical Logic

The controller uses an offset-based pagination strategy. Items are sorted by the `Date` field in descending order (`-Date`) so the newest uploads always appear first.

- **Total:** Represents every document matching the criteria in your collection.
    
- **Skip:** Calculated as $(page - 1) \\times 12$. If you are on page 2, the API skips the first 12 items.
    
- **Limit:** Hardcoded to `12` to ensure consistent grid layouts on the frontend.
    

---

### 🧪 Sample Testing in Postman

1. Set method to **GET**.
    
2. Enter the URL: `{{base_url}}/api/getAllgallery?page=1`.
    
3. **Check the** **`total`** **field:** This tells you how many total items exist across all pages.
    
4. **Check the** **`data`** **array:** This contains the 12 most recent gallery entries.

This endpoint retrieves the full details of a specific gallery item using its unique database ID. It is useful for displaying a dedicated detail page or a full-screen gallery view.

4. **Hit Send.**

### Delete Gallery Entry (DELETE)

This endpoint permanently removes a gallery record from the database and **automatically deletes** all associated image files (the `coverImage` and the `images` array) from the server's disk to save storage space.

- **URL:** `{{base_url}}/api/deleteGallery/:id`
    
- **Method:** `DELETE`
    
- **Auth:** `Bearer Token` (Required)
    
- **Permissions:** `admin`, `user`
    

---

### 🔍 Path Parameters

Replace `:id` in the URL with the unique `_id` of the gallery entry you wish to remove.

| **Parameter** | **Type** | **Example Value** | **Description** |
| **`id`** | String | `65d8f2a1b3c4d5e6f7g8h9i0` | The MongoDB ObjectID of the entry. |

---

### 🛠 Behind the Scenes: Cleanup Logic

Unlike a standard delete, your controller performs a "Deep Delete":

1. **Find:** Locates the document to get the file paths.
    
2. **Unlink:** Loops through the `coverImage` string and the `images` array to delete the actual `.jpg` or `.png` files from the `/public/images/GaImageGallery` folder.
    
3. **Remove:** Deletes the document from MongoDB.
    

---

### ✅ Success Response (200 OK)

JSON

```
{
  "status": "success",
  "message": "Gallery entry and associated files deleted successfully."
}

 ```

---

### ❌ Possible Errors

| **Status Code** | **Message** | **Scenario** |
| **404** | `No Document found with ID ...` | The ID is valid but does not exist in the database. |
| **401** | `Unauthorized` | No token provided or token has expired. |
| **403** | `Forbidden` | You are logged in, but your role is not "admin" or "user". |
| **400** | `Invalid ID: ...` | The ID string is malformed (e.g., `123-abc`). |

---

### 🧪 Sample Testing in Postman

1. Set the method to **DELETE**.
    
2. In **Headers**, ensure `Authorization` is set to `Bearer` .
    
3. Enter the URL: `{{base_url}}/api/deleteGallery/65d8f2a1b3c4d5e6f7g8h9i0`.
    
4. **Hit Send.**
    
5. _Verification:_ Try to "GET" the same ID; it should now return a **404**.

- `descriptionOne`, `descriptionTwo`, `discriptionThree`, `discriptionFour` (optional)
    
- `status` (enum: `draft` / `published`, default `draft`)
    

> 

Automatically parses `tags` string into an array if sent as `"AI, Tech, Science"`.

### Headers

| --- | --- |

| OR |  |

# Service Search API Documentation

## Overview

The Service Search API allows clients to search services by title. The search is case-insensitive and supports partial matching, returning all services whose titles contain the specified keyword.

---

# Endpoint

## Search Services by Title

**HTTP Method**

`GET`

**Endpoint**

``` text
/api/service/search

 ```

**Note:** If your application uses the plural route (`/api/services`), replace `/api/service` with `/api/services`.

**Full URL Example**

``` text
http://localhost:8000/api/service/search?title=cloud

 ```

---

# Request Parameters

## Query Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| title | String | Yes | Keyword used to search the service title. |

### Example Request

``` http
GET /api/service/search?title=cloud

 ```

---

# Headers

| Key | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Content-Type | application/json |

> <p >Authentication headers may be required if your API is protected.</p> 
  

---

# Successful Response

## HTTP Status Code

`200 OK`

## Response Example

``` json
{
    "status": "success",
    "results": 2,
    "data": {
        "services": [
            {
                "_id": "66ab1234567890abcdef1234",
                "imageCover": "uploads/Services/cover.jpg",
                "images": [
                    "uploads/Services/image1.jpg",
                    "uploads/Services/image2.jpg"
                ],
                "catagory": "Technology",
                "status": "active",
                "title": "Cloud Infrastructure",
                "description": "Cloud infrastructure consulting and implementation.",
                "subTitleOne": "Assessment",
                "subdescriptionOne": "Evaluate your existing infrastructure.",
                "subTitleTwo": "Migration",
                "subdescriptionTwo": "Migrate applications securely.",
                "headLine": "Cloud Solutions",
                "createdDate": "2026-07-15T08:30:00.000Z"
            }
        ]
    }
}

 ```

---

# No Matching Results

If no service matches the search keyword, the API returns an empty collection.

## HTTP Status Code

`200 OK`

## Response Example

``` json
{
    "status": "success",
    "results": 0,
    "data": {
        "services": []
    }
}

 ```

---

# Error Responses

## 1\. Missing Title Parameter

### HTTP Status Code

`400 Bad Request`

### Request

``` http
GET /api/service/search

 ```

### Response

``` json
{
    "status": "fail",
    "statusCode": 400,
    "message": "Please provide a title to search."
}

 ```

### Reason

The required `title` query parameter was not provided.

---

## 2\. Invalid Request

### HTTP Status Code

`400 Bad Request`

### Response Example

``` json
{
    "status": "fail",
    "statusCode": 400,
    "message": "Invalid request."
}

 ```

### Reason

The request contains invalid or unsupported parameters.

---

## 3\. Internal Server Error

### HTTP Status Code

`500 Internal Server Error`

### Response Example

``` json
{
    "status": "error",
    "message": "Something went wrong. Please try again later."
}

 ```

### Reason

An unexpected server-side error occurred while processing the request.

---

# Search Behavior

The search:

- Is case-insensitive.
    
- Supports partial keyword matching.
    
- Searches only the **title** field.
    
- Returns all matching services.
    

### Examples

Searching for:

``` text
cloud

 ```

Matches:

``` text
Cloud Infrastructure
Cloud Migration
Cloud Security Services

 ```

Searching for:

``` text
consulting

 ```

Matches:

``` text
Business Consulting
Technology Consulting
IT Consulting Services

 ```

---

| KEY | VALUE |

| title | cloud |

``` text

 ```

---

# Notes

- The endpoint performs a read-only search and does not modify any data.
    
- Search is performed only on the **title** field.
    
- The search supports partial and case-insensitive matching.
    
- The `results` property indicates the number of matching services returned.
    
- If no matching services are found, the API returns **200 OK** with an empty array.
    
- This endpoint is intended for searching services by title only.

# Team Search API Documentation

## Overview

The Team Search API allows clients to search team members by name. The search is case-insensitive and supports partial matching, returning all team members whose names contain the specified keyword.

---

# Endpoint

## Search Team Members by Name

**HTTP Method**

`GET`

**Endpoint**

``` text
/api/team/search

 ```

**Full URL Example**

``` text
http://localhost:8000/api/team/search?name=john

 ```

---

# Request Parameters

## Query Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| name | String | Yes | Keyword used to search the team member's name. |

### Example Request

``` http
GET /api/team/search?name=john

 ```

---

# Headers

| Key | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Content-Type | application/json |

> 

**Note:** Authentication is **not required** for this endpoint unless configured differently in your application.

 
  

---

# Successful Response

## HTTP Status Code

`200 OK`

## Response Example

``` json
{
    "status": "success",
    "results": 2,
    "data": {
        "teams": [
            {
                "_id": "66ab1234567890abcdef1234",
                "image": "uploads/Teams/john.jpg",
                "name": "John Smith",
                "specialty": "Software Engineer",
                "status": "Active",
                "socialMedia": [
                    {
                        "platform": "LinkedIn",
                        "url": "https://linkedin.com/in/johnsmith"
                    },
                    {
                        "platform": "Facebook",
                        "url": "https://facebook.com/johnsmith"
                    }
                ],
                "createdDate": "2026-07-16T08:30:00.000Z"
            }
        ]
    }
}

 ```

---

# No Matching Results

If no team member matches the search keyword, the API returns an empty collection.

## HTTP Status Code

`200 OK`

## Response Example

``` json
{
    "status": "success",
    "results": 0,
    "data": {
        "teams": []
    }
}

 ```

---

# Error Responses

## 1\. Missing Name Parameter

### HTTP Status Code

`400 Bad Request`

### Request

``` http
GET /api/team/search

 ```

### Response

``` json
{
    "status": "fail",
    "statusCode": 400,
    "message": "Please provide a team member name to search."
}

 ```

### Reason

The required `name` query parameter was not provided.

---

## 2\. Invalid Request

### HTTP Status Code

`400 Bad Request`

### Response Example

``` json
{
    "status": "fail",
    "statusCode": 400,
    "message": "Invalid request."
}

 ```

### Reason

The request contains invalid or unsupported parameters.

---

## 3\. Internal Server Error

### HTTP Status Code

`500 Internal Server Error`

### Response Example

``` json
{
    "status": "error",
    "message": "Something went wrong. Please try again later."
}

 ```

### Reason

An unexpected server-side error occurred while processing the request.

---

# Search Behavior

The search:

- Is case-insensitive.
    
- Supports partial keyword matching.
    
- Searches only the **name** field.
    
- Returns all matching team members.
    

### Examples

Searching for:

``` text
john

 ```

Matches:

``` text
John Smith
Johnson Adams
John Doe

 ```

Searching for:

``` text
alex

 ```

Matches:

``` text
Alex Brown
Alexander Wilson

 ```

---

# Postman Configuration

`GET`

``` text

 ```

| KEY | VALUE |
| --- | --- |
| name | john |

``` text

 ```

# Notes

- The endpoint performs a read-only search and does not modify any data.
    
- Search is performed only on the **name** field.
    
- The search supports both partial and case-insensitive matching.
    
- The `results` property indicates the number of matching team members returned.
    
- If no matching records are found, the API returns **200 OK** with an empty array.
    
- This endpoint is intended solely for searching team members by name.
